answer: In an AI agent economy, each participant must forge a unique identity by locking scarce computational work and capital before joining markets. A monitoring raven continuously scans interaction graphs for dense clusters of low-reputation accounts that fail to demonstrate durable resource commitments. Agents that pass these checks earn a jade-colored trust badge reflecting sustained stake. Sybil attackers incur massive costs because every fake identity demands repeated proof-of-work and locked funds that cannot be recycled cheaply, rendering large-scale identity farms economically unviable.
